name: Release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        description: current releases package.json; patch/minor/major open a validated release PR.
        required: true
        type: choice
        options:
          - current
          - patch
          - minor
          - major
      source_sha:
        description: Exact merged release source; automation only, normally left blank.
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Prepare ${{ inputs.bump }} release
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
      issues: read
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      ready: ${{ steps.release.outputs.ready }}
      version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}
      sha: ${{ steps.release.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Require the default branch
        env:
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF" != "refs/heads/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then
            echo "::error::Run releases from $DEFAULT_BRANCH, not $GITHUB_REF_NAME"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Check out release history
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          fetch-tags: true

      - name: Select trusted release source
        env:
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ inputs.source_sha }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SOURCE_SHA" ]; then
            exit 0
          fi
          if [[ ! "$SOURCE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Release source must be a full commit SHA"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git cat-file -e "$SOURCE_SHA^{commit}"; then
            echo "::error::Release source $SOURCE_SHA is not available"
            exit 1
          fi
          default_sha=$(git rev-parse "origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH")
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$SOURCE_SHA" "$default_sha"; then
            echo "::error::Release source $SOURCE_SHA is not merged into $DEFAULT_BRANCH"
            exit 1
          fi
          git checkout --detach "$SOURCE_SHA"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Grep-level enforcement of the architectural seams (AGENTS.md "Respect the
# seams"). This is a coarse backstop that complements the precise ESLint rules
# in eslint.config.mjs — it catches a violation even if lint is skipped, and
# documents the invariants in one readable place.
#
set -uo pipefail

fail=0
SRC="src"

report() {
  # $1 = human description, $2 = matching lines (empty = ok)
  if [[ -n "$2" ]]; then
    printf '\033[31m✗ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"
    printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed 's/^/    /'
    fail=1
  else
    printf '\033[32m✓ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"
  fi
}

# 1. ipcRenderer only in the preload bridge.
hits=$(grep -rnw 'ipcRenderer' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/preload/' || true)
report "ipcRenderer used only in src/preload/" "$hits"

# 2. Host primitives (fs / child_process / chokidar / node-pty) only in LocalHost.
hits=$(grep -rnE "from ['\"](node:)?(fs|fs/promises|child_process)['\"]|from ['\"](chokidar|node-pty)['\"]|import\(['\"]((node:)?(fs|fs/promises|child_process)|chokidar|node-pty)['\"]\)" \
  "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/project-host/local-host.ts' || true)
report "host primitives imported only in local-host.ts" "$hits"

# 3. PTY spawning (host.spawnPty call sites) only in the supervisor.
hits=$(grep -rnE '\.spawnPty\(' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/pty/pty-supervisor.ts' || true)
report "host.spawnPty() called only in pty-supervisor.ts" "$hits"

# 4. Bundled harness identities stay inside provider-owned main modules. Shared

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run policy, type, and test verification
        env:

  electron-smoke:
    name: Electron smoke (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run production Electron workflow
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/production
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke

      - name: Run development renderer Performance Timeline containment
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/development-performance
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke:development-performance

      - name: Prove failure and interruption isolation
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke:isolation

      - name: Upload bounded Electron failure evidence
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ci-electron-smoke-failure-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  macos-electron-smoke:
    # Temporary reduced gate: terminal-presentation, terminal-lifecycle, and capacity
    # remain available through local commands while their macOS flakes are hardened.
    name: Electron correctness (macOS arm64; temporary reduced gate)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run focused unpackaged Electron scenarios
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/macos-ci
        run: npm run smoke:macos:ci

      - name: Upload bounded macOS Electron failure evidence
        if: failure()

/**
 * `ProjectHost` — the transport seam (ADR-010).
 *
 * Every filesystem, exec, PTY, and watch operation in hvir goes through a
 * `ProjectHost`. `LocalHost` is the default implementation; `SshHost` (Phase 4)
 * will implement the same interface over ssh2. Nothing above this seam knows or
 * cares whether a project is local or remote — remoteness is transport, not a
 * server. All paths are host-qualified `HostPath`s.
 */

import type { Duplex } from 'node:stream'

import type {
  HostId,
  HostPath,
  DirEntry,
  Stat,
  WatchEvent,
  ExecResult,
  HostConnectionState,
  HostWatchTier,
  Disposer,
  LoopbackEndpoint,
  TextWorkload,
} from '../../shared'

export type { Disposer }

/** Maximum UTF-8 payload accepted by one duplex exec-stream write. */
export const MAX_EXEC_STREAM_WRITE_BYTES = 256 * 1024

export interface ExecOptions {
  readonly cwd?: HostPath
  readonly env?: Record<string, string>
  /** Remove inherited variables before applying `env`. */
  readonly unsetEnv?: readonly string[]
  /** Written to the child's stdin before the stream is exposed. */
  readonly input?: string
  /**
   * Keep stdin open for `ExecStreamHandle.write()` / `.end()`.
   *
   * Streaming stdin remains closed by default so existing commands that read
   * until EOF cannot hang. Buffered `exec()` always ignores this option and
   * closes stdin after `input`.
   */
  readonly keepStdinOpen?: boolean
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
  /** Max bytes to buffer across stdout+stderr before failing. */
  readonly maxBuffer?: number
  /** Terminate and return the buffered prefix instead of rejecting at maxBuffer. */
  readonly allowTruncatedOutput?: boolean
  /** Also terminate after this many NUL-delimited stdout records. */
  readonly maxStdoutNulRecords?: number
}

export interface ExecStreamHandle {
  onStdout(cb: (chunk: string) => void): Disposer
  onStderr(cb: (chunk: string) => void): Disposer
  onError(cb: (error: Error) => void): Disposer
  onExit(cb: (result: { code: number | null; signal: string | null }) => void): Disposer
  /** Write one bounded UTF-8 payload, resolving after the transport accepts it. */
  write(data: string): Promise<void>
  /** Optionally write one final bounded payload, then close stdin. */
  end(data?: string): Promise<void>
  kill(signal?: string): void
  dispose(): void
}

export interface WatchOptions {
  readonly recursive?: boolean
  /**
   * Additional host-qualified roots owned by the same backend. They follow the
   * same depth policy as `path`; callers use this to keep UI-driven shallow
   * interests bounded without consuming one SSH channel per directory.
   */
  readonly additionalPaths?: readonly HostPath[]
  /** Directory basenames to prune entirely from a recursive watch. */
  readonly excludeDirectoryNames?: readonly string[]
  /** Watch backends report asynchronous failures here instead of throwing. */
  readonly onError?: (error: Error) => void

#!/bin/bash
set -e

stage='configuring the hvir command'
report_failure() {
  status=$?
  echo "hvir package configuration failed while $stage" >&2
  exit "$status"
}
trap report_failure ERR

HVIR_COMMAND='/opt/${sanitizedProductName}/resources/hvir-command'
chown root:root "$HVIR_COMMAND"
chmod 0755 "$HVIR_COMMAND"
if command -v update-alternatives >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [ -L '/usr/bin/${executable}' ] &&
    [ -e '/usr/bin/${executable}' ] &&
    [ "$(readlink '/usr/bin/${executable}')" != '/etc/alternatives/${executable}' ]; then
    rm -f '/usr/bin/${executable}'
  fi
  update-alternatives \
    --install '/usr/bin/${executable}' '${executable}' \
    "$HVIR_COMMAND" 100
else
  ln -sf "$HVIR_COMMAND" '/usr/bin/${executable}'
fi

stage='configuring the Chromium sandbox helper'
chown root:root '/opt/${sanitizedProductName}/chrome-sandbox'
if command -v runuser >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
  runuser -u nobody -- unshare --user true >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  chmod 0755 '/opt/${sanitizedProductName}/chrome-sandbox'
else
  chmod 4755 '/opt/${sanitizedProductName}/chrome-sandbox'
fi

stage='refreshing desktop metadata'
if command -v update-mime-database >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  update-mime-database /usr/share/mime
fi

{"path":"/private/var/tmp/ws/0d79d7fe/hvir/README.md","file_text":"# hvir

hvir is a desktop workbench for local and remote software projects. It keeps
file browsing, viewing, Git, terminals, and coding-agent sessions in one
Electron app so you can work a repository without switching tools for each
surface.

Version `0.2.3`. Requires Node.js 24 or later.

## Features

- **Projects and workspaces.** Open multiple projects. Git worktrees become
  workspaces you can switch, close, and prune.
- **Local and SSH hosts.** The same workbench talks to a local filesystem or a
  remote host over SSH. Paths stay host-qualified.
- **File tree.** Create, rename, move, copy, delete, and reveal files. Search
  by filename. Git status decorates the tree.
- **Viewer.** Source (CodeMirror), rendered (Markdown, Mermaid, HTML, JSON,
  YAML, CSV, images), and Git diffs. Find, go-to-line, blame, and split tabs.
- **Git rail.** Working-tree changes, history, commit graph, branch switch,
  fetch, and pull. Mutations run through an authorized coordinator.
- **Terminals.** Ghostty-based panes with splits, themes, search, clipboard,
  and attention badges. PTY lifetime is owned by main, not the renderer.
- **Harnesses.** Launch a login shell or a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex,
  Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Pi) with per-provider profiles,
  probes, and session recovery where the provider supports it.
- **Document review.** Comment on source or rendered documents and insert or
  send the review into a trusted harness composer.
- **Sessions.** Overview of live terminals across workspaces, with detail and
  foreground focus.
- **Web panes and HTML preview.** Embed trusted web surfaces; untrusted HTML
  runs in a sandboxed custom-protocol origin.
- **Diagnostics.** Workbench health, diagnostic reports, and renderer recovery.

Packaged installers currently target **macOS arm64** (`.pkg`) and **Linux**
x64/arm64 (`.deb`, glibc ≥ 2.35).

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 24
- npm (this repository uses `package-lock.json`)
- A native toolchain so `postinstall` can rebuild `node-pty` and
  `@hvir/rename-noreplace` against Electron
  - macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools
  - Linux: a C/C++ toolchain (`build-essential` or equivalent) and Python for
    `node-gyp`

## Getting started

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd hvir
npm ci
npm run dev
```

`npm ci` installs dependencies and rebuilds native modules for Electron.
`npm run dev` starts electron-vite with hot reload.

Optional: install the repository Git hooks so pushes run typecheck plus the
local-platform Electron smoke suite.

```bash
npm run hooks:install
```

Bypass with `git push --no-verify` when you intentionally skip that gate.

## Common scripts

| Script | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Development Electron app |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck and production electron-vite build |
| `npm run preview` | Preview the production renderer |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` for Node and web projects |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint, including architectural import bans |
| `npm run format` / `npm run format:check` | Prettier |
| `npm test` | Vitest unit tests (Node, not Electron) |
| `npm run test:watch` | Vitest watch mode |
| `npm run verify` | Seams, ADRs, architecture budgets, lint, typecheck, tests |
| `npm run smoke` | Packaged-path Electron smoke scenarios (Linux default) |
| `npm run smoke:macos` | macOS smoke subset |
| `npm run smoke:scenario -- <name>` | One smoke scenario |
| `npm run pack:mac:arm64` | macOS `.pkg` |
| `npm run pack:linux:x64` / `pack:linux:arm64` | Linux `.deb` |

`npm run verify` is the contributor gate CI runs on Linux. Electron smoke is a
separate job (`xvfb-run` on Linux).

## Layout

```
src/main/        Electron main process (hosts, PTY, Git, IPC, windows)
src/preload/     Typed `window.hvir` bridge — the only ipcRenderer user
src/renderer/    React workbench UI
src/shared/      Cross-process types and IPC contracts
src/workers/     Isolated Git and echo workers
packages/        Native addons (`@hvir/rename-noreplace`)
scripts/         Seams, architecture, smoke, packaging, release
test/            Vitest coverage for seams and UI logic
build/           Icons, entitlements, package scripts
```

Important seams, enforced by ESLint and `npm run check-seams`:

- Host primitives (`fs`, `child_process`, `chokidar`, `node-pty`) live only in
  `src/main/project-host/local-host.ts`. Everything else goes through
  `ProjectHost`.
- Only the PTY supervisor may call `host.spawnPty()`.
- The renderer never imports `ipcRenderer`; it uses `window.hvir`.
- Bundled harness identities stay inside `src/main/harness/`.

Git work and other CPU-heavy host work can run in `src/workers/` so the main
process stays responsive.

## Testing

Unit tests do not start Electron. They cover HostPath, LocalHost, Git, harness
policy, renderer hooks, and similar seams:

```bash
npm test
```

Smoke tests build a smoke-channel Electron app and drive real workbench
scenarios (PTY, viewer, Git, SSH workspace, web pane, sessions, terminals):

```bash
npm run smoke
```

On Linux without a display, use Xvfb (`xvfb-run -a npm run smoke`). Mutation
testing is available as `npm run test:mutation` (Stryker).

## Packaging

Production artifacts are written to `dist/` by electron-builder.

```bash
npm run pack:mac:arm64
npm run pack:linux:x64
npm run pack:linux:arm64
```

Installed packages expose a `hvir` command that can open a project directory:

```bash
hvir .
```

Linux packages install under `/opt/hvir` with an AppArmor profile. macOS
packages install to `/Applications/hvir.app` with Hardened Runtime
entitlements.

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Bundled third-party notices, including the
ghostty-web terminal runtime and the rename-noreplace binding, are in
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

# hvir

A desktop workbench for software projects that unifies file management, code viewing, Git workflows, terminals, coding agents, SSH remotes, and document review in one place."},{"type":"text","content":"I have enough context to write a README covering the workbench, setup, scripts, and architecture."},{"type":"tool_call","id":"call-358b79db-8520-4065-a57f-66165b78fadd-96","name":"create","arguments":{"path":"/private/var/tmp/ws/0d79d7fe/hvir/README.md","file_text":"# hvir

hvir is a desktop workbench for local and remote software projects. It keeps
file browsing, viewing, Git, terminals, and coding-agent sessions in one
Electron app so you can work a repository without switching tools for each
surface.

Version `0.2.3`. Requires Node.js 24 or later.

## Features

- **Projects and workspaces.** Open multiple projects. Git worktrees become
  workspaces you can switch, close, and prune.
- **Local and SSH hosts.** The same workbench talks to a local filesystem or a
  remote host over SSH. Paths stay host-qualified.
- **File tree.** Create, rename, move, copy, delete, and reveal files. Search
  by filename. Git status decorates the tree.
- **Viewer.** Source (CodeMirror), rendered (Markdown, Mermaid, HTML, JSON,
  YAML, CSV, images), and Git diffs. Find, go-to-line, blame, and split tabs.
- **Git rail.** Working-tree changes, history, commit graph, branch switch,
  fetch, and pull. Mutations run through an authorized coordinator.
- **Terminals.** Ghostty-based panes with splits, themes, search, clipboard,
  and attention badges. PTY lifetime is owned by main, not the renderer.
- **Harnesses.** Launch a login shell or a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex,
  Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Pi) with per-provider profiles,
  probes, and session recovery where the provider supports it.
- **Document review.** Comment on source or rendered documents and insert or
  send the review into a trusted harness composer.
- **Sessions.** Overview of live terminals across workspaces, with detail and
  foreground focus.
- **Web panes and HTML preview.** Embed trusted web surfaces; untrusted HTML
  runs in a sandboxed custom-protocol origin.
- **Diagnostics.** Workbench health, diagnostic reports, and renderer recovery.

Packaged installers currently target **macOS arm64** (`.pkg`) and **Linux**
x64/arm64 (`.deb`, glibc ≥ 2.35).

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 24
- npm (this repository uses `package-lock.json`)
- A native toolchain so `postinstall` can rebuild `node-pty` and
  `@hvir/rename-noreplace` against Electron
  - macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools
  - Linux: a C/C++ toolchain (`build-essential` or equivalent) and Python for
    `node-gyp`

## Getting started

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd hvir
npm ci
npm run dev
```

`npm ci` installs dependencies and rebuilds native modules for Electron.
`npm run dev` starts electron-vite with hot reload.

Optional: install the repository Git hooks so pushes run typecheck plus the
local-platform Electron smoke suite.

```bash
npm run hooks:install
```

Bypass with `git push --no-verify` when you intentionally skip that gate.

## Common scripts

| Script | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Development Electron app |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck and production electron-vite build |
| `npm run preview` | Preview the production renderer |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` for Node and web projects |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint, including architectural import bans |
| `npm run format` / `npm run format:check` | Prettier |
| `npm test` | Vitest unit tests (Node, not Electron) |
| `npm run test:watch` | Vitest watch mode |
| `npm run verify` | Seams, ADRs, architecture budgets, lint, typecheck, tests |
| `npm run smoke` | Packaged-path Electron smoke scenarios (Linux default) |
| `npm run smoke:macos` | macOS smoke subset |
| `npm run smoke:scenario -- <name>` | One smoke scenario |
| `npm run pack:mac:arm64` | macOS `.pkg` |
| `npm run pack:linux:x64` / `pack:linux:arm64` | Linux `.deb` |

`npm run verify` is the contributor gate CI runs on Linux. Electron smoke is a
separate job (`xvfb-run` on Linux).

## Layout

```
src/main/        Electron main process (hosts, PTY, Git, IPC, windows)
src/preload/     Typed `window.hvir` bridge — the only ipcRenderer user
src/renderer/    React workbench UI
src/shared/      Cross-process types and IPC contracts
src/workers/     Isolated Git and echo workers
packages/        Native addons (`@hvir/rename-noreplace`)
scripts/         Seams, architecture, smoke, packaging, release
test/            Vitest coverage for seams and UI logic
build/           Icons, entitlements, package scripts
```

Important seams, enforced by ESLint and `npm run check-seams`:

- Host primitives (`fs`, `child_process`, `chokidar`, `node-pty`) live only in
  `src/main/project-host/local-host.ts`. Everything else goes through
  `ProjectHost`.
- Only the PTY supervisor may call `host.spawnPty()`.
- The renderer never imports `ipcRenderer`; it uses `window.hvir`.
- Bundled harness identities stay inside `src/main/harness/`.

Git work and other CPU-heavy host work can run in `src/workers/` so the main
process stays responsive.

## Testing

Unit tests do not start Electron. They cover HostPath, LocalHost, Git, harness
policy, renderer hooks, and similar seams:

```bash
npm test
```

Smoke tests build a smoke-channel Electron app and drive real workbench
scenarios (PTY, viewer, Git, SSH workspace, web pane, sessions, terminals):

```bash
npm run smoke
```

On Linux without a display, use Xvfb (`xvfb-run -a npm run smoke`). Mutation
testing is available as `npm run test:mutation` (Stryker).

## Packaging

Production artifacts are written to `dist/` by electron-builder.

```bash
npm run pack:mac:arm64
npm run pack:linux:x64
npm run pack:linux:arm64
```

Installed packages expose a `hvir` command that can open a project directory:

```bash
hvir .
```

Linux packages install under `/opt/hvir` with an AppArmor profile. macOS
packages install to `/Applications/hvir.app` with Hardened Runtime
entitlements.
